articles.title: Akshay Kumar's simple food habits: Why dal, roti and vegetables can beat a complicated diet
articles.summary: Wellness News: Akshay Kumar has built a reputation as one of Bollywood’s fittest stars well into his late 50s. While many chase the latest superfoods, protein powder.
articles.body: Akshay Kumar has built a reputation as one of Bollywood’s fittest stars well into his late 50s. While many chase the latest superfoods, protein powders or complicated meal plans, the actor keeps things refreshingly simple. Reports and interviews repeatedly show that his everyday meals often centre around classic Indian staples like dal, roti and seasonal vegetables.In one candid conversation on the show Wheels of Fortune he even said that the real joy of a Gujarati thali with its dal, sabzi and roti simply cannot be matched by avocado toast or fancy pastas. Akshay’s approach is not about deprivation. It is about trusting food that has nourished generations.Here is why a plate of dal, roti and vegetables can quietly outperform the most elaborate modern diets.It delivers complete, balanced nutrition without the fussA simple thali of dal, whole-wheat roti and mixed vegetables packs protein, complex carbohydrates, fibre, vitamins and minerals in one go. A good bowl of dal can give about 12 grams of protein a couple of rotis can add a few more grams and the sabzi will give you more fiber and micro nutrients. Together they make a meal that feels satisfying and keeps the body fueled for hours. Unlike diets that demand constant tracking of macros or expensive ingredients, this combination works because the foods complement each other naturally.According to the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), pulses represent an important component of healthy diets.Akshay’s preference for these everyday foods lines up with what nutritionists observe: when the plate is filled with familiar, unprocessed items, people tend to stick with the habit for years instead of quitting after a few weeks of complicated rules.It supports better digestion and a healthier gutComplicated diets often load the system with processed items, artificial sweeteners or sudden high-fibre supplements that can leave the stomach uncomfortable. Dal and vegetables, on the other hand, provide natural fibre that feeds the good bacteria in the gut.Studies comparing traditional Indian plant-based patterns with more Westernised eating have found that the former is linked to a more diverse and healthier gut microbiome. People who stay closer to dal, sabzi and whole grains tend to show lower markers of gut inflammation.Akshay has long spoken about giving the stomach proper rest through early dinners and occasional fasting. When the main meals are already light on spices, onion and garlic (as his sattvic-leaning choices often are) and rich in easily digested plant foods, the digestive system works with less strain. That quiet daily support adds up over decades.It keeps blood sugar steady and energy levels evenFad diets frequently swing between extreme carb restriction and sudden high-sugar “cheat” days. Dal has a naturally low glycaemic index because of its fibre and protein content. When eaten with whole-wheat roti and vegetables, the meal releases glucose slowly into the bloodstream. This prevents the sharp spikes and crashes that leave people reaching for snacks or feeling drained by afternoon."Someone like Akshay needs to keep his physical energy high for action sequences and long hours of shooting. He therefore needs this constant fuel. He does not need constant supplements or complicated timing of meals; the food itself does most of the work.It is sustainable, affordable and easier to live with for lifeThe biggest advantage of dal, roti and vegetables is that almost every Indian kitchen already knows how to cook them. There is no need for imported powders, special apps or weekly meal-prep stress. When a diet feels like home food rather than a temporary project, people stay consistent.People who stick to balanced, plant-forward meals built around pulses, whole grains and vegetables enjoy better weight management, lower risk of chronic lifestyle diseases and greater overall well-being compared with those cycling through short-term complicated plans.Also read: Rakul Preet Singh’s honest gym comeback: “Teaching your body old tricks feels like a new job”Also read: Preity Zinta’s shoulder injury leaves her ‘Demoralised’, but she is slowly finding her way backGet the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates. articles.title: Motociclista avança sinal, bate em ônibus e garupa morre em Jundiaí  | G1
articles.standfirst: Acidente ocorreu no cruzamento das ruas Rangel Pestana e Siqueira de Moraes, no Centro de Jundiaí (SP). Condutor foi socorrido e levado ao Hospital São Vicente de Paulo.
articles.summary: Um motociclista avançou o sinal vermelho, bateu em um ônibus e seu garupa morreu na madrugada desta segunda-feira (7), em Jundiaí (SP).
articles.body:
Um motociclista avançou o sinal vermelho, bateu em um ônibus e seu passageiro que estava na garupa morreu, na segunda-feira (7), em Jundiaí (SP).

O acidente aconteceu no cruzamento entre as ruas Rangel Pestana e Siqueira de Moraes, na região central.

Motociclista avançou o sinal vermelho, bateu em um ônibus e seu garupa morreu em Jundiaí (SP), na madrugada desta segunda-feira (7) — Foto: Departamento de Trânsito de Jundiaí/Divulgação

Com o impacto, o passageiro sofreu ferimentos graves e morreu no local.

O condutor da moto foi socorrido e encaminhado ao Hospital São Vicente de Paulo.

Jundiaí registrou outro acidente grave no domingo (6), na Rodovia Geraldo Dias (SP-332). Um motorista, que discutia com a companheira, invadiu a contramão e bateu de frente com outro carro.

Com o impacto, duas pessoas ficaram presas às ferrangens, foram socorridas e levadas ao Hospital São Vicente de Paulo, em Jundiaí (SP) — Foto: Departamento de Trânsito de Jundiaí/Divulgação

Com o impacto, duas pessoas ficaram presas às ferrangens, foram socorridas e levadas ao Hospital São Vicente de Paulo.

Segundo a Polícia Militar, os dois motoristas envolvidos estavam bêbados.

No domingo (6), um motorista bêbado, que discutia com a companheira, acabou invadindo a contramão — Foto: Departamento de Trânsito de Jundiaí/Divulgação

articles.title: Shiv Sena leader Rahul Gharat arrested in Palghar hospital doctor assault case
articles.summary: PALGHAR: Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palgh.
articles.body: PALGHAR: Shiv Sena (Shinde faction) Palghar city chief Rahul Gharat, the main accused in the alleged ruckus and assault at a private hospital in Palghar, was arrested on Monday after he surrendered before the police.The incident took place at Relief Hospital in Palghar on Saturday night when five injured Govindas, who had sustained injuries during Dahi Handi celebrations, were admitted for treatment. Three of them were kept in the intensive care unit (ICU).The injured Govindas had alleged that the hospital was forcing them to undergo CT scans and was trying to charge them excessive amounts. Following the allegations, Shiv Sena office-bearers and workers entered the hospital late at night and allegedly created a ruckus. A hospital employee was assaulted and the IV lines of the Govindas admitted to the ICU were allegedly removed before they were taken away.Palghar police had registered a case against 17 people, including Shiv Sena district chief Kundan Sankhe, city chief Rahul Gharat, the son of MLA Rajendra Gavit and deputy taluka chief Rohit Gavit, under various sections of the law.“Gharat appeared before the Palghar police station on Monday and was arrested. Efforts are on to trace the remaining accused,” said Kishor Manbhav, senior police inspector of Palghar police station.Meanwhile, injured Govinda Akash Patil reiterated his allegations against the doctors. He claimed that although he felt better after being given an injection, he was allegedly kept in the ICU for three hours after being put on a saline drip against his wishes. He demanded action against the doctors.MLA seeks action against doctorsPalghar MLA Rajendra Gavit visited the Palghar police station on Monday and demanded that a case be registered against the doctors.Gavit alleged that the hospital staff were forcing the injured Govindas to stay back and undergo MRI and CT scans. He said Shiv Sena workers had gone to the hospital to help the injured Govindas and that a verbal altercation had taken place.He alleged that the doctors had filed a complaint against the Shiv Sena workers out of vendetta and pressured the police to register a case. “Can a patient not even question a doctor about an excessive bill?” Gavit asked, demanding that the police register a case against the doctors.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Thane | Silver Rate in Thane | Bank Holidays in Thane | Public Holidays in Thane | Petrol Price in Thane | Diesel Price in Thane | CNG Price in Thane | LPG Price in ThaneStay updated with the latest Thane news.
